**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Logic (0590), Paper 2, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B. ONLY THE FIRST FIVE QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

All the questions carry 20 marks. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets.

enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B: PROBLEM-SOLVING**

**4.** *Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:*

> The Logic students of G.B. H. S held a meeting to examine their study strategies. At the end of the session, they agreed to be very serious, attend classes regularly and form study groups. When the meeting was over, the staff equally had a meeting with all examination students to advise and orient them in their studies. During the meeting, some students raised a worry concerning the lack of notes and some basics needs.
>
> The college counselor advised that, success is a result of joint effort of teachers and parents. If parents support their children and teachers teach well, success will be guaranteed. So, either parents or teachers are responsible for students' failure.
>
> One of the students wondered aloud, "but what is a college?". "It is an institution of higher learning" said the counselor. In conclusion, the principal stated that, "teachers are always guardians. Most parents do not guide". It is clear that since most parents are irresponsible, every parent is irresponsible.

**Questions:**
incertitudes: Q4(a)(i) : « General Term and Collective Term » : plusieurs réponses acceptables dans le passage (« parents », « teachers » ; « staff », « study groups ») ; une est donnée, les autres citées. Q4(a)(ii) : « a kind of Definition » : la réponse de la principale (« institution of higher learning ») est classée définition par genre et différence (réelle) ; c'est aussi une définition lexicale.
Q4(b)(ii) : « Most parents are irresponsible » traduit en I (« Some ... ») selon la logique traditionnelle ; une forme « Most S are P » n'existe pas dans le carré des oppositions.

Q4(c) : conclusion « Some parents are not teachers » (AOO-2, Baroco) ; les prémisses sont lues dans l'ordre imprimé, majeure d'abord. Validité recalculée avec Python (avec et sans import existentiel).

Q4(d)(ii) : « Fallacy of Composition from the passage » : le passage conclut de « most parents » à « every parent » ; c'est le sophisme retenu (composition / généralisation hâtive, passage de la plupart à tous). Aucune autre phrase du passage ne le porte plus clairement.
Q4(e)(ii) : le sujet impose les variables p, q et r pour (i) et (ii) ; (ii) n'a besoin que de deux variables, avec des significations redéfinies.
Transcription du passage : orthographe imprimée conservée (« counselor », « some basics needs », « G.B. H. S »).

Aucun corrigé officiel ; les corrigés sont des réponses modèles de manuel de logique traditionnelle (définitions, règles de distribution, carré des oppositions avec import existentiel, ordres de l'enthymème : 1er = majeure supprimée, 2e = mineure supprimée, 3e = conclusion supprimée). Les tables de vérité, la validité des syllogismes (AOO-2, EOO-1, EIO-4) et du dilemme sont recalculées avec Python. À faire relire par un enseignant de logique : les définitions varient d'un manuel à l'autre.

Règle de choix : la page de garde dit « Answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B ; only the first five questions answered will be marked ». Section A (questions 1 à 3) : toutes obligatoires, donc aucune règle ; Section B (questions 4 à 6) : `parmi 2 sur 3`. La règle « les cinq premières réponses seules sont corrigées » est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.
Points : chaque question est imprimée « 20 marks » ; chaque sous-question (a) à (e) vaut 4 points (« 2 x 2 marks », sauf Q2(a) imprimée « 4 x 1 marks »). 5 x 4 = 20 : aucun écart de somme.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Identify from the passage a General Term and a Collective Term.

(ii) Select a kind of Definition from the passage. (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) General term:** "parents" (also "teachers", "students", "guardians"): a term that applies in the same sense to each member of a class of things. **Collective term:** "staff" ("the staff equally had a meeting"): a term that names a group taken as a whole (also "study groups" or "the college"); it applies to the group, not to each member separately.

**(ii) Kind of definition.** The counselor's answer to "what is a college?", "It is an institution of higher learning", is a **definition by genus and difference** (a real, logical definition): "institution" is the genus and "of higher learning" is the specific difference. It is also a **lexical (reportive)** definition, since it reports the usual meaning of the word.
themes: O Level Logic - definition and division

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Translate the following Propositions into their Optimum Logical Forms:

(i) *Every parent is irresponsible.*

(ii) *Most parents are irresponsible.* (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The optimum logical form is the standard form (A, E, I or O) with quantifier, subject term, copula and predicate term.

**(i)** "Every parent is irresponsible" is a **universal affirmative (A)**: **All parents are irresponsible persons.**

**(ii)** "Most parents are irresponsible" asserts that more than half, so at least some, parents are irresponsible, and does not say that all are; in traditional logic "most" is treated as particular, so it is a **particular affirmative (I)**: **Some parents are irresponsible persons.**
themes: O Level Logic - propositions and their types
O Level Logic - symbolic logic basics

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) From the following premises, derive a suitable conclusion:

*All teachers are guardians.*

*Some parents are not guardians.*

*Therefore* ................................

(ii) Determine the Mood of the Syllogism in c (i) above. (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Terms: teachers (T), guardians (G), parents (P). The term "guardians" is the **middle term** (it is in both premises and not in the conclusion). The first premise is the major premise (it contains the major term "teachers") and the second is the minor premise (it contains the minor term "parents"). Since the minor premise is negative (O), the conclusion must be negative and particular:

**Therefore, some parents are not teachers.**

Check: the middle term "guardians" is distributed in the minor premise (predicate of an O proposition), and "teachers", distributed in the conclusion (predicate of an O), is also distributed in the major premise (subject of an A). One premise only is negative and the conclusion is negative: the syllogism is valid.

**(ii) Mood.** The mood is the sequence of the types of the major premise, the minor premise and the conclusion: A (All teachers are guardians), O (Some parents are not guardians), O (Some parents are not teachers): **mood AOO**. The middle term is the predicate in both premises, so it is in the **second figure**: AOO-2 (the valid mood called *Baroco*).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Provide the Conclusion to the following argument to make it a Modus Ponens:

*If teachers teach well, then success is guaranteed.*

*Teachers teach well.*

*Therefore* ................................

(ii) Identify a Fallacy of Composition from the passage. (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** In a modus ponens the minor premise affirms the antecedent, so the conclusion affirms the consequent: **Therefore, success is guaranteed.** Form: $p \supset q$, $p$, $\therefore q$.

**(ii)** The fallacy of composition consists in attributing to a whole or to every member of a class a quality that is true only of some of its parts or members. In the passage it is the final statement: **"since most parents are irresponsible, every parent is irresponsible"**. What is true of most parents (they do not guide) is wrongly passed on to all parents without exception.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) Using the variables p, q and r, symbolise the following statements:

(i) *If parents support their children and teachers teach well, success will be guaranteed.*

(ii) *"Either parents or teachers are responsible for student's failure".* (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Let $p$ = parents support their children, $q$ = teachers teach well, $r$ = success will be guaranteed. The statement is a conditional whose antecedent is a conjunction:

$$(p \cdot q) \supset r$$

**(ii)** Let $p$ = parents are responsible for students' failure and $q$ = teachers are responsible for students' failure. The statement is a disjunction:

$$p \vee q$$

(The variable $r$ is not needed here; if one wishes to use the three variables of part (i) one must define new meanings for them.)
themes: O Level Logic - symbolic logic basics
O Level Logic - propositions and their types
